title: Belief-Mapping Operationalization of Inversion Principle
summary: Operationalizes the Inversion Principle through belief-mapping questions ("What would I need to believe for [the alternative] to be right?") as the primary form, amending ADR-010's cross-cutting application from four locations to six by adding PLAY and SYNTHESIS. The Cycle 9 spike found adversarial framing ("strongest case against X") overcorrected 2-6x by activating Compliance Dynamics, while belief-mapping achieved near-zero preference-driven divergence; adversarial framing is deprecated as the default operationalization but remains available when the user explicitly requests it.
workflow_point: cross-cutting: RESEARCH, PRODUCT DISCOVERY, DECIDE, ARCHITECT, PLAY, SYNTHESIS
mechanism: belief-mapping question form ("what would I need to believe for X to be right?")

links.note: Amends ADR-010: expands the Inversion Principle's cross-cutting application from four locations to six (adding PLAY and SYNTHESIS) and specifies belief-mapping as the mandatory operationalized form.
Applies belief-mapping, one of the six research-grounded question forms cataloged in ADR-056, as the Inversion Principle's mandatory primary operationalization.
